page: Amazon Web Services m8a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AMD EPYC 9R45 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores running at speeds up to 4.5 GHz, without multi-threading enabled on the core topology (1 thread per core). Cache allocation comprises 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). Vector and algorithmic acceleration features include AVX-512 extensions (such as AVX512F, VNNI, and BF16) along with AES and SHA cryptographic extensions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core computational characteristics. In Geekbench tests, the m8a.xlarge achieves a single-core score of 2,827.0, ranking in the top tier alongside top-tier stress-ng single-core performance (3,771.19), single-threaded gzip compression (41.42 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (18.16 GB/sec). Text generation on small language models (135M) also scores in the top tier at 363.76 tokens per second. Multi-core performance metrics, such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 8,922.0, PassMark CPU score of 13,568.14, and stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 15,047.94, settle into the middle tier, directly reflecting the 4-core physical limit.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the absence of dedicated GPUs and local storage, meaning all persistent storage workflows rely exclusively on network-attached EBS volumes. Network performance is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. While the DDR5 memory subsystem delivers sustained uncached read bandwidth of 53.47 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 34.44 GB/sec, large-scale parallel processing is limited by total thread count. The server provides balanced resource density and high per-core execution speed, making it suitable for web application hosting, mid-sized relational database operations, CI/CD compilation, and lightweight CPU-based microservice architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores on a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 x86_64 processor and 16.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes AVX-512 instruction support alongside 16 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local disk storage, relying on networked storage over a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, and contains no hardware accelerators. Benchmark testing shows top-tier single-core CPU throughput, text generation on small LLM models, and single-threaded compression, balanced by median multi-core and memory subsystem results. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, the instance is engineered for general-purpose workloads, including web servers, application runtimes, code compilation, and database backends requiring high single-thread clock rates.
